resolutions.rationale: Sense 1 is defined around a person suspected of crime or wrongdoing. The unqualified “suspicions about 〈person/behavior〉” frame can instead express the general distrust defined in Sense 2, so it was removed from Sense 1. This keeps the trust-based sense distinct without duplicating an unsupported frame.

The original use note included unexplained situations and any feeling that “something is wrong,” which can also fall under Sense 3. It was narrowed to a person suspected of crime or wrongdoing and the pattern now names a wrongdoing that-clause. Oxford’s Sense 1 examples include arouse suspicion in a police context; the specific fraud example remains aligned with Sense 1.
